MENA

June 14, 2026

The US and Iran are reported to be close to finalising a significant diplomatic agreement that could reshape regional relations.
The potential deal would reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a critical global shipping lane, to unrestricted passage.
Tehran has responded to the announcement with caution, signalling reservations about the emerging accord.
Israel's Prime Minister has sought to distance himself from the agreement, receiving the news coolly.
President Donald Trump says the two nations are on the verge of signing what he describes as a "great settlement."

The US and Iran announced that they had reached a memorandum of understanding aimed at ending the current conflict and launching negotiations on a final peace agreement, laying the groundwork for weeks of intensive talks.

The agreement, expected to be signed this week in Switzerland, would reopen the Strait of Hormuz and lift a US blockade. It would also bring an end to hostilities across regional fronts, including in Lebanon.
